requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: A 4096-bit RSA key and a self-signed X.509 root CA certificate were generated with subject/issuer CN=OS Comparison Root CA, CA:TRUE critical basic constraint, keyCertSign/cRLSign key usage, valid 10 years. Command output directly confirms subject and issuer.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: The CA cert was copied into /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and update-ca-trust extract was run. 'trust list' shows the cert present as an anchor/authority and openssl verify against the system tls-ca-bundle succeeds. A signed test leaf certificate also verified successfully against the system bundle without specifying the CA explicitly, directly demonstrating system-wide trust. This state was also confirmed to persist after a node reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (98aa35f5-...) and healthy CA trust state were captured, systemctl reboot was issued with acknowledgement, subsequent polls show connection timeout/reset consistent with the node being down, then a new boot_id (c7e930f4-...) was observed confirming an actual reboot, and post-restart checks show the CA anchor, key file, and trust verification all recovered. This is corroborated by the fixed before_prepare/after_executor global boot-identity snapshots, which show the identical boot_id transition (98aa35f5-... to c7e930f4-...).

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — creating a root CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' and installing it as a trusted system CA — are directly and coherently evidenced, including end-to-end trust verification via a signed test leaf certificate. The independently required node-restart protocol was also fully and correctly executed and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, showing a genuine boot_id transition and recovered CA trust state post-reboot. No unnecessary mutations or residue were found.
limitations: The full command list confirms 14 commands were run (11 successful, 3 with connection-loss outcomes during reboot); none of the failures represent unaddressed task problems.
Preparation phase was a no-op (prepare disabled), so before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are identical aliases and provide no additional differentiation.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task outcomes: CA key/cert generation (cmd-b06b313e372e4c6e, cmd-a49bd5e2f497488d), installation into the system trust anchors plus update-ca-trust extract (cmd-2148f406c5f04e12), a bounded end-to-end test leaf certificate created in /tmp for verification (cmd-f35540b51c474d8c) that was fully cleaned up immediately afterward (cmd-d391e35c0e6e4261, which also removed the CA .srl serial file), and the mandated reboot (cmd-7a29d8f304d64fea). The fixed after_executor temporary-files snapshot shows only the expected reboot.log and post-reboot systemd-private directories, with no leftover leaf certificate or CSR files, and failed-services and package-health remained clean before and after. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
